title: Latvian voters moved a party’s last-listed candidate up to 4th, and its 4th down to last
body: On 3 October 2026 Latvia elected its parliament, the Saeima, and its voters did more than pick parties. Each party’s list is its own ballot paper, and beside every name are a green “for” box and a red “against” box, which a voter may mark or leave blank, as the public broadcaster LSM [explains](https://eng.lsm.lv/article/politics/election/02.09.2026-latvian-saeima-elections-2026-how-the-election-works.a658525/). A candidate’s votes are the list’s ballots plus the for marks minus the against marks, and the list’s seats go to its highest totals, whatever order the party printed. In Rīga, according to the [Central Election Commission](https://dati.cvk.lv/SV2026/en/velesanu-rezultati/kandidatu-saraksti/progresivie/), 34,294 voters chose the Progressives’ list: Kaspars Briškens, printed 4th, got 2,841 for and 6,502 against marks and fell to 43rd, while Mārtiņš Hiršs, printed 43rd, got 4,577 for and 856 against and rose to 4th, taking one of the list’s 6 seats. The marks never change how many seats a party wins, because a ballot counts once for its list, marked or not.

slides.prompt: In Rīga, Jānis Urtāns of Latvia’s United List got 1,815 “for” and 3,097 “against” marks from voters in October 2026. Did he win a seat?
slides.answer: Yes: he rose from 28th on the list to 9th of its 13 seats.
slides.detail: 38 of the list’s 43 names got more against than for marks, so the seats went to the 13 with the highest totals: the list’s 84,160 ballots plus for minus against.

slides.alt: Animation on dark carmine: a fan of 14 Latvian ballot papers, one per party list, with green for and red against boxes beside the names; a count of ballots plus for minus against; a ladder of 43 names where No. 4 falls to last and No. 43 rises to 4th; tiles for the United List.

slides.prompt: Get Candidate F, printed last, into one of the list’s 2 seats without giving F a single “for” mark.
slides.takeaway: Against marks on four rivals do it: only the order of the totals counts. In Rīga in 2026, 38 of the United List’s 43 names had more against than for, and the seats went to the 13 highest totals.

slides.heading: Progressives in Rīga: votes = 34,294 ballots + for − against
slides.note: Central Election Commission of Latvia. 6 seats: Burāne came 6th, Briškens 43rd of 43.

slides.heading: How a Latvian ballot paper is counted

steps.label: Choose one party’s list as your ballot
Mark names for or against, if you like
Ballots + for − against rank its names
The highest totals take the seats

slides.question: In Latvia’s 2026 parliamentary election, what did a red “against” mark next to a candidate’s name do?
options: Took one vote off that candidate
Moved the vote to another party
Counted only if most voters agreed
slides.explanation: Each ballot gives every name on its list one vote; a for mark adds one and an against mark takes one off. The party’s total, and so its number of seats, stays the same.

source.label: Central Election Commission of Latvia: 2026 Saeima election results
